name: Invisible Collar Guard Reset
summary: The Invisible Collar holder unloads the neck, opens the high-leg clinch, and restores a facing bottom guard with inside frames before selecting another attack.
description: The Invisible Collar holder unloads the neck, opens the high-leg clinch, and restores a facing bottom guard with inside frames before selecting another attack.
overview:
The Invisible Collar holder unloads the neck, opens the high-leg clinch, and restores a facing bottom guard with inside frames before selecting another attack.

Begin as the bottom holder of the Invisible Collar high-leg enclosure. Release all neck pressure before changing the high-leg connections.

Open the enclosure through the hips while keeping the raised knees comfortable and supported. Retain inside frames as the legs lower so you remain facing the opponent. Restore ordinary Closed Guard/Bottom when the distance permits the ankles to close comfortably. If the ankles cannot close, recognize Open Guard/Bottom instead of forcing the high enclosure back together.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Invisible Collar Guard Reset Defender
defender.description: Recognize Invisible Collar Guard Reset and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Let all neck pressure release before moving through the opening. Keep a balanced base as the high legs lower. Retain inside arm position without twisting a captured shoulder. Recognize ordinary closed guard when the legs close around the waist. Face the remaining open guard when the ankles stay apart.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

flashcards.answer: Let all neck pressure release before moving through the opening.

flashcards.question: Against Invisible Collar Guard Reset, when must you stop moving?
flashcards.answer: Stop at a tap, verbal signal, distress, or a loaded joint or neck. Release before changing direction.

flashcards.question: Against Invisible Collar Guard Reset, does interrupting one grip guarantee a new position?
flashcards.answer: No. Confirm the remaining body and leg controls before claiming the guard, pin, or submission has changed.
